question: Inference task tickets (one file per inference call, ~280/day, 49MB so far, never pruned) push every proof sandbox past the 150MB bound. Should they (a) be kept, and the proof snapshot leave their contents out the way it already leaves out logs/ (recommended: no learning data lost, sandbox cost stops growing with call volume), (b) be logging class, deleted after 30 days, or (c) something else?
why_it_blocks: Measured 2026-10-02: test_isolation reds at 150.1MB against ticket 1c4ae8f053fe's 150MB per-proof sandbox bound, so the tester component is red and no tester ticket (e038 first) can cross to PROVED. ae8d/0bcd already cut 127MB of unread mail; it crept back. The largest grower is ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets: 1386 files, 49MB, oldest 2026-09-17, ~280 new per day, no retention rule anywhere, and the only reader is the probe are_inference_task_tickets_complete. A fixed MB bound over a growing instance-space will keep reddening until the growth has a rule.
answer: lets talk about the intention for those task tickets. they are a logging artifact, so the intention is that they wind up in the logging tree. their consumers are: learning loops. if we make a change to our learning, we don't have to rerun the inference calls, we can relearn off the same data. second, if we discover an issue, we have the complete history of inference for the last 30 days, a complete log trail for each call. Forensic levels of information that should allow us to resolve issues without running the thing again. It's already worked 3 times in that role.
